premise: When my mother died, her will bequeathed me a $190,000 collection of rare first-edition children’s books, but my older brother, the executor, forged a codicil that left the collection to his daughter and told me my mother had disinherited me; later I found an email where he offered to sell a signed ‘Wizard of Oz’ to a dealer. I hired a probate attorney, proved the codicil was fake, and recovered the collection — I now operate a children’s literacy nonprofit called ‘Turned Pages,’ where children earn books from the collection by reading, and I’ve trademarked a logo featuring my brother’s name crossed out with ‘Dishonest Executor’ underneath.
